findings.explanation: The SPL has no hourly bin or two-period persistence check. It counts matches per host/camera_id/error_code over the whole scheduled window and fires on count > 5. A reader tuning from this text would expect behaviour the search does not have.
findings.quote: alert when Splunk counts failures/hour stay above five for two rolling hours per camera
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the actual logic (more than 5 matching PTZ error lines per camera and error_code in the search window), or ask the SPL owner to add `bin _time span=1h` plus a two-consecutive-hour check and then keep this sentence.

findings.explanation: In the SPL, preset, Home, timeout and motor are free-text search keywords, not fields. The only fields the search needs are host, camera_id and error_code, and events lacking error_code or camera_id are silently dropped by `stats ... by`. detailedImplementation repeats the same requirement.
findings.quote: with Splunk-extracted fields **`preset`**, **`home`**, **`timeout`**, **`motor`**, and **`error_code`** tied to **`camera_id`**
findings.suggested_fix: State that the raw PTZ log lines must contain the keywords (preset, home, timeout, motor, stall, 'PTZ error'), and that camera_id and error_code must be extracted (error_code normalised via lookup) for the event to be counted.

findings.explanation: SC4S is a containerised syslog-ng service deployed on its own Linux host near the sources, which sends events to Splunk over HEC. It is not an app installed on, or the usual companion of, a heavy forwarder.
findings.quote: Splunk Connect for Syslog ([Splunkbase app 4740](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4740)) on a hardened Heavy Forwarder is the usual pattern
findings.suggested_fix: Say: deploy SC4S on a dedicated Linux host in the camera/VMS VLAN, sending to Splunk HEC; alternatively, use a heavy forwarder with a TCP/UDP or TLS syslog input.

findings.explanation: These read like product integration names, but there is no evidence that Axis Companion or Device Manager forwards PTZ homing/preset diagnostics, or that a 'Hanwha diagnostic bridge' exists as a product. Most cameras instead support a remote syslog server directly.
findings.quote: Milestone Recording Server bridges, Axis Companion/Device Manager feeds, Hanwha diagnostic bridges, or Hikvision SDK exporters
findings.suggested_fix: Check each vendor's documentation for which PTZ fault messages are logged and how they are exported (camera remote syslog, VMS event/alarm API). Name only confirmed mechanisms and the actual message text for preset/home failures.

findings.explanation: I could not confirm this page exists; the forwarding/receiving topics live under the Forwarding manual and syslog inputs under Data/Monitornetworkports. The docs site returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches.
findings.suggested_fix: Open the URL in a browser; if it 404s, replace it with https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/Data/Monitornetworkports.

findings.explanation: The sentence is dense and hard to act on: 'bodies' (camera housings) and the claim that Device Pack release notes define PTZ error integers are unclear and unsupported.
findings.quote: Tier diagnostics verbosity on noisy Axis/Hanwha/Hikvision bodies first; normalize vendor integers into **`error_code`** via transforms lookup tables Milestone administrators align with Device Pack release notes.
findings.suggested_fix: Split into concrete steps: reduce PTZ log verbosity outside calibration; build an error_code lookup from each vendor's documented PTZ fault codes (cite the source); and apply it via automatic lookup.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The title promises 'Auto-Flip Failure' monitoring, but the SPL keyword filter (preset, Home, timeout, motor, stall, 'PTZ error') contains no auto-flip/flip token and nothing else in the UC describes auto-flip events.

No time binning, so 'count > 5' depends on the schedule window rather than a stated rate. The bare keyword `Home` will match unrelated lines (for example web UI 'home' page requests) in nvr:diagnostic.

summary: Exclusions, evidence and visualization are specific to PTZ cameras. However, the implementation's 'two rolling hours' persistence rule and the title's auto-flip failures are not in the SPL, dataSources presents search keywords as extracted fields, and the collection guidance mislocates SC4S on a heavy forwarder.
